reformulation: Capacity-forced binary zeros plus exact auxiliary substitution: 1,758/351 -> 1,682/301 vars/rows, 6,379 -> 6,125 nonzeros. At chain position 95 the load is provably >= 21 while z#95 <= 25, so 26 of group 31's choices (x#31#70..95) are forced to zero; all 50 continuous s#j, their 50 defining c02 equalities and 50 c03 rows are replaced by delay#j >= sum_t (t-r_j)x#j#t, the exact combination c03_j+c02_j+r_j*c04_j after deleting proved-zero columns. Claimed as a bijection of feasible points with pointwise objective preservation on the 1,682 retained coordinates.
claim_class: 3 claims, no single bijection rule: forward (reverse=false, integer both sides, objective Equal, inverse=1 = identity for all input coordinates) plus reverse integer (inverse=0) plus reverse LP inclusion (input/output_integers=false, inverse=null). The zeros are the only non-linear content: 26x Round+EqPair on a hand-derived capacity fact.
claims: Claim 0 (reverse=false, integer, inverse=1): 8,537 checks = 1,682 VarLower + 1,682 VarUpper + 1,431 VarInt refs + 198 RowEq refs + 179 Local (103 changed rows + 26 zero-column inverse steps + 50 recovery refs) + 3,365 literal 'Exact'; 259 steps = 207 Lin + 26 Round + 26 EqPair; 1,682-entry Return map (62,828 B).

Claim 1 (reverse=true, integer, inverse=0): 8,689 checks = 1,682+1,682 bounds + 1,431 VarInt + 251 RowEq refs + 150 Local + 3,493 Exact, over a 1,758-entry map (81,773 B) and 150 Lin steps (79,405 B).
Claim 2 (reverse=true, integers false, inverse=null): 5,550 checks; adds no step and only removes the 1,457 VarInt refs and 1,682 inverse checks of claim 1 - target LP inclusion into the source LP.

All three projections are the same 1,682-pair source->target index table (17,986 B, identity on only 54 pairs); claims[0] uses the pair order, claims[1..2] the transposed order (tools/prepare_test76.py:61). request.json is byte-equal to the claims array plus a newline (54,290 B, verified against the RPA's copy).

Zero proof shape: one 7-term capacity Lin, then per removed column a 232-term scaled Lin (cap at 1/5 plus VarLower premises c/5) rounded through {"VarInt": x} to x<=4/5, then EqPair(x<=0, {'VarLower': x}) (tools/prepare_test76.py:21-24); RPA sample {"Round":{"id":3,"le":{"Local":2},"integer":{"VarInt":701}}}.
proof_encoding: proof.rpa = 'RPA 2'+newline+one JSON certificate {claims,blocks}, 920,390 B; request.json re-serializes the same claims array (54,289 B inside the RPA, 54,290 B in the file); proof.rpx 709,068 B; VERIFIED at 22,776 obligations / 282,306 work units / 0 branches in 19.6 ms (cases/test76/preparation.json, README).

Block sizes are lopsided: block 0 = 351,750 B (259 steps, all 26 Round and 26 EqPair), blocks 1 and 2 = 274,996 B and 239,185 B (150 Lin each), so the whole zero/first-order argument lives in one block.

Measured duplication: blocks 1 and 2 have byte-identical step lists (79,405 B) and byte-identical Return maps (81,773 B); they differ only in checks (8,689 vs 5,550), i.e. 161,178 B of the 920,390 B RPA is verbatim text repeated.

Step shapes: one 96-term prefix-sum chain c00_1+c01_1..c01_95, one 7-term capacity Lin, 26 Lins of 232 terms each, 50 recovery Lins, 103 row-identity Lins of 2-64 terms; 4,993 of block 0's 8,537 obligations are direct model refs and 3,365 are the string 'Exact'.

Resource pressure is nil: 0.9 MB RPA vs a 256 MiB text limit, 282,306 work vs 1e9; the cost of this case is the ~600 lines of shared Python that assembled it and the manual derivation behind it, not the artifact.
agent_manual_work: Two hand-written MPS decoders (token parser plus a strict fixed-field re-decoder) and a canonical fixed-field MPS writer for the target; digest eval 'Writing and auditing final MPS artifact' re-decoded the written bytes and matched every intended coefficient, sense, RHS, bound, marker and objective coefficient.

Derived the capacity witness itself: exact cumulative load rows for all 201 positions, per-group mandatory contributions at every position, unique mandatory maximum 21 at position 95, full scan of all 1,457 options yielding exactly 26 refutable choices (group 31, indices 70-95), then a re-run after deletion with 0 further rounds (digest evals 'Checking exhaustive forced-load implications', 'Inspecting residual-capacity structure').

Built the 50 substitution certificates by hand: the exact combination c03_j+c02_j+r_j*c04_j per group, the proof that r_j <= sum_t t*x#j#t follows from the group's own domain and bounds, and the zero-column cancellation in every changed row (digest eval 'Certifying intended exact reformulation').

Audited its own artifact: token vs field parser agreement, all 52 c01 + 50 c03 + 1 c04 changed rows, all retained rows, duplicate-row and incidence-component scans, and wrote audit.json (215,129 B) plus report.md (10,146 B) with both hashes.

No framework member was touched (solver-blind baseline run); 14 eval cells / 34,893 chars of hand-rolled exact arithmetic over fractions.Fraction and collections.Counter, with 18 turns, 0 failing tool calls, 434 s wall.
preparer_helpers: tools/prepare_test76.py is 97 lines and imports 10 helpers from 6 sibling preparers: parse_mps/row_ref (prepare_affine:20,77), expression/plus/mul/expr_json/row_fact/sha (prepare_test40:72-89), substitute (prepare_test57:11), SparseBuilder (prepare_test70:14), fact/box (prepare_test54:20,26), rounded (prepare_test84:15) - 1,107 lines in total for one certificate.

SparseBuilder.lin (prepare_test70:21-31) is the entire emission layer: appends {'Lin':{id,kind,constant,terms}}, asserts the exact residual against the expected expression and allocates ids; prepare_affine's own parse_mps (:20) is a second full MPS reader.
rounded (prepare_test84:15-20) is the zero-forcing kernel: asserts the Le premise and the Int premise have identical support (a[1]==z[1]), ceil-rounds the constant and emits exactly one Round step.

box/fact (prepare_test54:20,26-33) collapse trivial obligations: box rewrites a coordinate-bound obligation into a VarLower/VarUpper premise ref after asserting ceiling<=0, and fact returns the existing model ref when the wanted expression already equals that fact - hence the 4,993 direct refs and 3,365 'Exact' strings.

Three hand-built tables carry the whole argument: definitions/groups/recoveries keyed by audit hint keys (:25-31), the 5-entry mandatory-group dict taken from the untrusted audit for the capacity combination (:21), and the (back,integer) claim loop that emits claims and blocks in one pass (:33-69).
friction: Blocks 1 and 2 replay byte-identical 79,405 B step lists and 81,773 B maps; the LP claim adds nothing and only drops 1,457 VarInt refs and 1,682 inverse checks, so the same 150-step loop runs twice and 161,178 B of the RPA is duplicated text.

request.json (54,290 B) is exactly the claims array re-serialized, 99.4% of it three times the same 1,682-pair projection table (17,986 B, in two transposed orders); the RPA carries a second copy of the same array.

3,365 of block 0's 8,537 obligations are the literal 'Exact' and 4,993 are direct model refs; objective equality, all 1,682 projection identities and the 50 eliminated-coordinate inverse identities are asserted in the preparer's Python (:60,:62,:68) and never seen by the kernel.

The capacity argument is fed from the untrusted audit rather than derived: the five group->weight pairs come from h['zero_choice_proof']['mandatory_groups'] and position 95 is hard-coded as range(1,96) (:20-21), so no API finds the mandatory-load maximum, the support set or the multipliers.

The five INVALID receipts carry only status+message: two name an obligation ordinal ('obligation 8487', 'obligation 4873') and three name no claim, step or coordinate, so an error in a 22,776-obligation certificate cannot be traced back to the coordinate that produced it.
notes: Vocabulary verdict for this quiet case: the universal needs do the heavy lifting (RULE_BUILDERS for 559 hand-written steps, MODEL_READBACK because both chosen MCMs are re-parsed in Python, CLAIM_PLANNING because 22,776 obligations are a pure function of 3 flags), but two items are not universal restatements: (1) nothing in the kernel finds the multipliers of a derived fact - the capacity combination and the 50 replacement-row combinations are hand-found, and the sibling pattern test16.py:20-29 only divides an existing single row; (2) EDIT_AUDIT is real here because the entire edit list (dropped columns, mandatory groups, substitution certificates) is imported from audit.json and merely cross-asserted, so the compiler must be able to derive and, failing that, falsify the agent's audit. Bookkeeping worth copying: one shared capacity fact reused 26 times by rational scaling, trivial commitments collapsed to refs, one projection table reused across claims.
